# Reporter
1. Reporters report directly to the Head of Personnel.
2. Reporters may investigate around the station for new information regarding ongoing situations or new situations occurring on the station.
3. Reporters may request interviews with any crew member, and may record them using a Tape Recorder.
4. Reporters may use their handheld cameras or, if available, set up wireless cameras.
5. Reporters may wear the press armor on blue alert and above if reporting in areas that may place them at risk.
6. While wearing press equipment (holo-pin and armor), reporters may not engage in combat except in self-defense.
7. The HOP may temporarily or permanently revoke the reporter's work equipment or immediately demote them for SOP breaches.
8. Reporters should try to abide by the press guidelines to the best of their capabilities.
# Press Guidelines Guidelines for Reporter work behavior. Keep them in mind, and get your news running through the station!
## Press Equipment Reporters have some critical work equipment:
### The Consoles
The 'breaking news console' and 'news manager console' are the reporter's main work tools.
The news manager console is where you can write your news articles; here you send all the important information you want the crew to know. It supports rich text writing and allows for attaching one photo per article.
The breaking news console can be used to send a station-wide announcement; it should be used [bold]only to relay extremely important information[/bold] (e.g., regarding major health risks or unusually large-scale events).
### The handhelds
The 'reporter PDA' and 'tape recorder' are both extremely valuable information-gathering tools.
The reporter PDA allows you to take a photo when used, consuming one blank photograph that can be attached to your news articles.
The tape recorder allows you to record conversations using a cassette tape, and it can also automatically generate a transcript of your tape.
[italic]Remember: Misuse of tools is grounds for revocation of work equipment and, in extreme cases, demotion.[/italic]
## Text Structure
1. [bold]Headline.[/bold] Try to tell the reader what the article is about at first glance.
2. [bold]Body.[/bold] Explain what happened: who, what, where, and when. Keep it organized and avoid one-line or irrelevant articles.
3. [bold]Relay information.[/bold] Always finish with what the crew needs to know or do, such as areas to avoid, who to contact, ongoing risks, or what is happening around the station.
### Quick Tips
- Separate your writing into a [bold]header[/bold] and a [bold]body[/bold] that explains what happened. Do this every time. - If you have more than one theme in the same article, you can separate them with different headings. - Quote your sources when possible. Use interview recordings from your Tape Recorder when you have them, or name the person who gave you that information. - Keep facts and opinions apart. If you are giving an opinion, say so. - Mention the time and location of events (if possible) so readers can follow along. - Use rich text whenever possible, but do not overdo it. - If you can, remember to take photos! It's always great to have something visually appealing. - Proofread before posting. Do it well, do it once.
